record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: For each d, is the reverse-mathematical strength of the strong-tree version of the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem for d trees strictly weaker than the corresponding strength for d+1 trees?

evidence.quote: (4) Is the reverse math strength of the (strong tree version) Halpern-Läuchli Theorem for d trees strictly weaker than for d + 1-trees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

For a finitely branching tree T ⊆ ω^{<ω}, a subset S ⊆ T is a strong subtree of T if there is an infinite set L ⊆ ω of "levels" such that (i) every node of S has length belonging to L, (ii) S has a unique root, (iii) for every s ∈ S and every level ℓ ∈ L strictly greater than |s|, the set of immediate successors in S of s at level ℓ consists of all extensions of s at level ℓ in T whenever s is at a non-maximal chosen level in S (equivalently, S is closed under the tree structure level-by-level so that S is itself order-isomorphic, as a level tree, to ω^{<ω} restricted to its branching pattern), and (iv) S meets every level in L.

For a fixed integer d ≥ 1, let T_1, …, T_d be perfect, finitely branching trees (e.g. T_i = 2^{<ω}). The strong tree version of the Halpern–Läuchli theorem for d trees, denoted HL(d), is the statement: for every finite coloring c : ⋃_{n∈ω}(T_1(n) × ⋯ × T_d(n)) → k of the "level products" of T_1, …, T_d (where T_i(n) denotes the n-th level of T_i), there exist strong subtrees S_i ⊆ T_i (i = 1, …, d), sharing a common infinite set of levels L, such that c is constant on ⋃_{n∈L}(S_1(n) × ⋯ × S_d(n)).

The reverse-mathematical strength of a Π^1_2 statement φ over the base system RCA_0 is the equivalence class of φ under provable equivalence over RCA_0, partially ordered by implication over RCA_0.

Problem. For every integer d ≥ 1, is the reverse-mathematical strength of HL(d) strictly weaker (over RCA_0) than the reverse-mathematical strength of HL(d+1)? Equivalently, does RCA_0 + HL(d+1) prove HL(d) while RCA_0 + HL(d) fails to prove HL(d+1), for each d ≥ 1?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for the reverse-mathematical strength of the strong tree Halpern–Läuchli theorem stratified by the number of trees did not produce any source establishing a strict hierarchy or its collapse. Related work addresses Halpern–Läuchli at measurable and singular cardinals and the strength of the tree theorem for pairs, but the per-d reverse-math comparison appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Halpern–Läuchli theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Three versions SDd, DSd, SSd are defined; the strong-tree (SS) version is studied for d-many trees.
status_evidence.claim: The strong-tree version for d trees is a standard object of study; no per-d reverse-math hierarchy is stated.

status_evidence.title: The Halpern-Läuchli Theorem at a Measurable Cardinal
status_evidence.snippet: Consistency of the Halpern-Läuchli Theorem on d many κ-trees at a measurable cardinal κ, given the consistency of a κ+d-strong cardinal.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work concerns large-cardinal consistency by number of trees, not the reverse-mathematical strength comparison.
